szoveg_eredeti:
As artificial intelligence (AI) bubble vigilance continued, semiconductor stocks were dumped on the New York Stock Exchange over the weekend. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index plunged more than 10%, and the Nasdaq Composite returned its gains this year. In particular, risk aversion sentiment is growing across the stock market, with the S&P 500 index, which has been supporting the stock market based on the inflow of circular sales to economic defense stocks, falling for seven consecutive trading days for the first time since COVID-19. As a result, concerns are growing that the domestic stock market will also face a "Black Monday" on Monday, the 23rd.

On the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) on the 20th (local time), the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 48,147.33, down 1.93% from the previous day. On the same day, the S&P 500 fell 3.70% to 6910.39, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 5.28% to 22,617.73.

The Dow Jones and S&P 500 entered a correction phase, falling more than 10% from their previous highs. In particular, the S&P 500 fell for seven consecutive trading days, marking the longest decline in trading days since February 2020, when the COVID-19 pandemic began. The Nasdaq Composite has come down to a level where it has returned all of its annual gains this year.

The volatility index (VIX), known as the "fear index," rose 26.20% to close at 35.89, due to such a decline in stock prices in all directions. This is the highest level since April 2025.

The market plunge on this day is attributed to the fact that AI-related market sentiment instability is not easily subsiding rather than the emergence of new bad news.

Seo Sang-young, a researcher at Mirae Asset Securities, said, "The burden on the AI industry's high corporate value has been highlighted again as Antropics fell due to a public offering after being listed," adding, "The overall instability of semiconductors has expanded due to AMD's report on short selling in China and Nvidia's accounting survey of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission." In particular, hedge sales related to options also contributed to the plunge in stock prices as the expiration date of options in November overlapped on the same day.

Reflecting worsening market sentiment, semiconductor companies' stock prices fell particularly large. Major semiconductor stocks such as Nvidia (-14.01%) and Micron (-13.89%) all recorded double-digit declines. As a result, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index also plunged 10.73%.

Copper prices are also sluggish due to growing concerns that AI data center projects will be delayed after the U.S. midterm elections. According to the Korea Exchange, three-month futures for electric copper on the London Metal Exchange closed at $12,160 per ton on the 20th, down 2.92% from the previous trading day. Since the 4th, after the midterm elections, the fall has reached 13.37%.

Copper is used in all processes such as power generation, transmission, and use. When the economy improves, demand increases, and prices rise, and when a recession is expected, it served as a leading indicator and gained the nickname "Dr. Copper." Copper is used in large quantities to build AI data centers, and the "Blue Wave" in the U.S. midterm elections is analyzed to be a factor in the price decline.

Analysts say the domestic stock market is likely to start on a sharp decline on the 23rd as major indexes and indicators plunge. The recent strong selling of foreigners is considered to be a factor that increases the burden on the domestic stock market.

According to the trading status of each investor in the securities market from the 16th to the 20th, foreigners sold a net 4.5159 trillion won in the regular market and aftermarket. Institutions also sold 454.7 billion won during this period.

The top foreigners' weekly net selling stocks were Samsung Electronics (1.79 trillion won) and SK Hynix (94.1 billion won), with large semiconductor stocks. Kim Sung-no, a researcher at BNK Investment & Securities, said, "Antropic listing along with Nvidia issues affected the sharp decline in the global stock market. Other stocks have been sold to incorporate new listed stocks, which is a sign that U.S. market liquidity is not as good as before, he said. "Considering this deterioration in liquidity, foreign selling will continue in the Korean market for the time being."
